title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 8th Congressional District
area: Northeastern Pennsylvania, including Luzerne, Lackawanna (Scranton, Wilkes-Barre), Wayne, Pike, and Monroe counties.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground. Rob Bresnahan Jr. defeated then-incumbent Rep. Matt Cartwright (D) 50.7%-49.1% in 2024, and Donald Trump (R) carried the district 53.8%-45.4% over Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee named Cognetti to its "Red to Blue" program and the National Republican Congressional Committee named Bresnahan to its "Patriot" program.
Paige Cognetti was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary after Eric Stone did not make the ballot; Rob Bresnahan was unopposed in the Republican primary.

According to The Cook Political Report's Erin Covey, Democrats have focused on Bresnahan's history of stock trading in the House after he said he supported a ban on members doing so; between January 2025 and February 2026 he executed 650 trades. A representative for Bresnahan said he "has never traded his own stocks and an outside financial institution manages his investments." Republicans have focused on Cognetti's record as Scranton mayor, including a Politico report that she "helped secure a state grant for a new Fidelity Bank headquarters, where her husband's uncle sits on the board."

summary.text: Rob Bresnahan Jr. is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 8th District, elected in 2024 after defeating then-incumbent Matt Cartwright. Before Congress he was chief financial officer and CEO of Kuharchik Construction, an electrical contracting company. He serves on the Agriculture, Small Business, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Born in Kingston, Pennsylvania, in 1990; earned a B.S. in business administration from the University of Scranton in 2012.

Worked as chief financial officer and CEO of Kuharchik Construction, a commercial electrical contractor, and was owner of RPB Ventures, a real estate development company, before his election to Congress.

priorities.text: Campaign website says that during his tenure he "focused on cutting red tape, defending working families, and delivering results for his hometown region," citing his work on the Transportation and Infrastructure, Small Business, and Agriculture committees.
priorities.quote: focused on cutting red tape, defending working families, and delivering results for his hometown region

priorities.text: Campaigned in 2024 on banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks and introduced a House bill in May 2025 that would have forbidden the practice.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Small Business, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in the 2025-2026 Congress.

Introduced a House bill in May 2025 that would ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks, after campaigning on such a ban; a Philadelphia Inquirer analysis found he made 617 trades totaling $7.24 million in 2025. His office said the trades are handled by an outside financial adviser and that he has never traded his own stocks.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024, defeating incumbent Matt Cartwright 50.7% to 49.1%.

candidates.name: Paige Cognetti

summary.text: Paige Cognetti is the Mayor of Scranton, elected in 2020 as the first woman to hold the office, running as a political outsider after the previous mayor pleaded guilty to public-corruption charges. She launched her congressional campaign in September 2025 with an ad criticizing incumbent Rob Bresnahan's stock trading, and is running while completing her current term as mayor.

background.text: A native of Oregon, Cognetti worked on Barack Obama's 2008 presidential campaign and later as a member of the Treasury Department during the Obama administration, and worked briefly at Goldman Sachs in New York before moving to Scranton in 2016.
Served on the Scranton school board and as a special assistant to the Pennsylvania attorney general before being elected mayor.

Elected Mayor of Scranton in 2020, running as an independent with the slogan "Paige Against the Machine" after the prior mayor, Bill Courtright, pleaded guilty to conspiracy, bribery, and extortion and was sentenced to seven years in prison.

priorities.text: Launched her campaign attacking incumbent Rob Bresnahan's record of stock trading in Congress after he campaigned on banning it, saying he made 600 trades in a single year.
priorities.quote: Rob ran for Congress on a promise to ban stock trades. This year, he's already made 600 trades — 600. I'm running for Congress because people here deserve a lot better than a rich kid disrespecting our hard work and proud legacy.

priorities.text: Her campaign launch ad accused Bresnahan of "ripping Medicaid away from Pennsylvania families" by voting for the budget reconciliation bill known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, and criticized the timing of some of his stock trades relative to policy events.
priorities.quote: Sold Chinese stocks the week of a tariff. Buys missile stocks before a war, buys jet stocks before a big contract.

positions.summary: Campaign launch ad accused incumbent Bresnahan of cutting Medicaid coverage for Pennsylvania families by voting for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, implying opposition to those cuts.
positions.quote: ripping Medicaid away from Pennsylvania families by voting for President Donald Trump's budget bill

candidates.researchNotes: Her personal campaign website could not be reached (the domain names most associated with her name redirect to a National Republican Congressional Committee attack site); positions are drawn from her campaign launch video and news coverage. As Scranton mayor she has official actions on record, but a full account of her mayoral record was outside this basic-tier research budget.
